findings.summary: pools set writes any object with a string id into the config without validating the pool shape against pool.schema.json.
findings.failure_scenario: pools set --json '{"id":"codex:plan","kind":"nope","junk":1}' returns ok and overwrites the configured pool; later forecast/pools list read a malformed pool or fail with E_CONFIG. Tests only cover bad JSON and unknown id.

findings.summary: Explicit import of a wholly corrupt CLI file returns ok instead of failing (design item 4).
findings.failure_scenario: usage import --file garbage.txt --cli codex --pool <id> where the file contains only non-JSON text: readers silently return empty readings and the command returns {ok:true} with no change, indistinguishable from 'no reading'.

findings.summary: Keyless usage record derives idempotency_key from a 32-bit FNV hash of row content, which can merge distinct records.
findings.failure_scenario: Two different manual records that collide (or identical content at the same clock ms) get the same auto: key; the second call returns the first row as success and the second consumption is silently not booked.

findings.summary: Importing an older reading file overwrites a newer stored used_fraction and CLI reset_at.
findings.failure_scenario: Import a file with latest at=10:00, then an older file with latest at=yesterday: pools.json regresses to the old reading, forecast treats it as stale and the older reset_at is stored as source cli.
